summary: This manuscript describes a novel consumer-grade wearable approach, leveraging a self-supervised learning architecture for sports agnostic (basketball, running, soccer, and tennis) activity intensity features, that integrates with a heat balance approach to predict whole-body sweating rate. We collected whole-body sweating rates and analyzed data from 234 trials from 147 volunteers. Wet-bulb globe temperature ranged from 11 to 35 oC. Wearable triaxial accelerometry and chest-strap heart rate data were processed through a pretrained neural network to predict metabolic components for heat balance equations. For the independent validation set, the mean absolute error for predicted whole-body sweating rate was 0.08 L/h for basketball, 0.17 L/h for soccer, 0.00 L/h for tennis, 0.03 L/h for running with 0.03 L/h for all sports combined. The accounted-for variance (R2) for the whole-body sweating rate predictions were 0.76 for basketball, 0.73 for soccer, 0.82 for tennis, 0.94 for running and 0.79 for all sports combined. This study produced the following novel advancements: (1) first integration of wearable-derived activity features with a heat balance equation for sweat prediction; (2) first validated sport-agnostic wearable sweat prediction approach; and (3) first wearable method enabling a priori hydration management planning for exercise-heat stress conditions.
title: Sports agnostic whole body sweat rate prediction using consumer-grade wearables and biophysics-guided machine learning

summary: Extended reality (XR) is increasingly used in rehabilitation but its effectiveness in chronic respiratory conditions remains unclear. We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of experimental studies comparing XR-based interventions with usual care or alternatives. Searches were performed from inception to March 2025 and risk of bias was assessed by two independent reviewers. Fifteen experimental studies were included. XR-based interventions significantly improved 6-min walk distance (mean difference [MD] = 29.90 meters), forced vital capacity (MD = 0.37 liters), reduced dyspnea (standardized mean difference [SMD] = −0.61), anxiety (SMD = −2.08), and depression (SMD = −1.10), and improved quality of life (SMD = −1.87). No significant effects were observed for forced expiratory volume in one second percent predicted or fatigue. Subgroup analyses showed stronger effects in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and with comprehensive XR programs. Exercise-based XR improved quality of life only, while activities of daily living simulations improved forced expiratory volume in one second percent predicted, and nature-based interventions showed no significant benefit. Heterogeneity was substantial, but sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness of primary outcomes. XR-based rehabilitation may improve exercise capacity, symptoms, and quality of life, but larger multicenter trials are required to confirm long-term effectiveness and cost-effectiveness.
title: A systematic review and meta analysis of extended reality interventions for chronic respiratory conditions

summary: Distinguishing Group A streptococcus (GAS) pharyngitis from viral upper respiratory tract infections (URTIs) is critical for appropriate antibiotic use but remains difficult on symptoms alone. We developed and internally validated a multimodal artificial intelligence (AI) model fusing pharyngeal images (Swin Transformer) with clinical metadata via gradient boosting decision trees, using 6666 visits and 119,988 images from 44 facilities collected March 2023–August 2025. For discriminating GAS from non-GAS (influenza A/B, COVID-19), the fusion model achieved area under the curve (AUC) 0.917 (95% confidence interval 0.907–0.926), outperforming image-only (0.902), metadata-only (0.871) and proxy Centor/McIsaac scores. At a pre-specified high-specificity threshold (≥0.90) sensitivity was 0.761; simulations indicated antibiotic-prescription reductions of 23–56% across GAS prevalences of 5–20%. External validation and prospective evaluation are needed.
title: Multimodal AI for bacterial vs viral upper respiratory tract infection multicentre development and internal validation

summary: Mesial temporal lobe epilepsy (mTLE) is a common drug-resistant epilepsy. Temporal lobe resection is the most effective treatment, but postoperative recurrence and antiseizure medication (ASM) withdrawal remain major clinical challenges. Existing prediction tools are limited by endpoint specificity, restricted external validation, and lack of integration into sequential postoperative management pathways. We developed a sequential modelling strategy in mTLE, spanning recurrence prediction to ASM withdrawal risk stratification. In phase 1, postoperative recurrence models were developed and validated using 52 preoperative multimodal features in 1278 patients across cohorts 1–4 (three retrospective, one prospective). Five top-ranked models achieved AUCs of 0.926–0.932 (internal) and 0.830–0.931 (three external sets), with a three-tier (low/intermediate/high) risk stratification. In phase 2, ASM withdrawal recurrence models were developed and validated in 679 seizure-free, phase 1 low/intermediate-risk patients eligible for withdrawal across cohorts 5–8 (three retrospective, one prospective). Five top-ranked models achieved AUCs of 0.897–0.902 (internal) and 0.789–0.933 (three external sets), with risk stratification for individualized withdrawal estimation. Models showed good calibration, net clinical benefit, and SHAP-based interpretability. A research-based risk-estimation web tool was developed to support potential clinical translation. This promising modelling strategy integrates population-level risk stratification with individualized prediction, providing preliminary postoperative guidance: high-recurrence-risk patients may not be ideal for early ASM withdrawal despite seizure freedom, while low-risk patients may be considered for earlier withdrawal evaluation. Given the primarily retrospective design and relatively small phase 2 prospective cohort, further prospective external validation and clinical-impact studies are required before routine implementation.
title: Sequential framework for predicting postoperative recurrence and antiseizure-medication withdrawal risk in mesial temporal lobe epilepsy

summary: Providing targeted, quality-assured patient information is essential for informed and autonomous decision-making but remains resource-intensive when delivered face-to-face. Multimedia-supported informed consent may enhance patient understanding and satisfaction while reducing physician time by complementing, rather than replacing, direct interaction. Our PRISMA-based systematic review, aiming to enable clinicians to implement and evaluate such a supplement, identified 907 articles of which 110 reports from OECD countries were included, including 62 randomized controlled trials. Among studies assessing the outcomes of interest, 71% reported improved patient understanding with multimedia tools compared to standard consent, 41% reported increased patient satisfaction (none reported decreases), and 91% found reduced or unchanged patient anxiety. In synthesis, to the extent possible despite substantial heterogeneity, findings suggest benefits and potential efficiency gains, and we were able to derive recommendations. However, considerable methodological variability and limitations affecting internal validity highlight the need for high-quality head-to-head comparative studies to draw more robust conclusions.
title: Potential of multimedia-supported informed consent in clinical practice: a systematic review

summary: Healthcare cyberattacks and related data-security failures have divergent publicly observable legal consequences. A purposive corpus of 133 records from 24 countries maps civil litigation, regulatory enforcement, and selected incidents without located civil compensation claims. Litigation records concentrate in the United States. Uneven source coverage and nonpublic remedies limit comparison and preclude causal inference. Consistent reporting could improve understanding of accountability and patient redress.
title: Divergent legal consequences of cyberattacks on healthcare organizations worldwide

summary: Tumor boards, recurring meetings at hospital institutions, assemble cancer specialists (e.g., medical oncology and pathology) to discuss patient care. In this work, we formally define tumor board case summarization, options generation, and meeting outcome prediction as AI tasks. We study datasets from four medical institutions and evaluate state-of-the-art large language models (LLMs) from the DeepSeek, GPT, Gemini, and Qwen families using expert human assessment. Medical oncologists created ~9.6k reference texts and 16k human judgments across tasks. Clinicians rated LLM-generated case summaries 3.57–4.59 out of 5.0 across institutions, but recommendation generation remained more challenging, with average scores of 2.0–3.6. Clinical alignment analyses showed modest correlations of ~0.2 for case summarization subtasks and higher correlations of ~0.6 for recommendation generation using LLM-as-Judge metrics. Our proposed TBFact metrics were competitive with LLM-as-Judge approaches in longer prose free-text settings, suggesting a promising direction toward explainable evaluation. This study, to our knowledge the largest expert-grading study of tumor board tasks with both granular and direct assessments, found that criterion-level scores and overall judgments are related nonlinearly. Experts also frequently assigned high ratings to responses that differed substantially from their reference texts, challenging assumptions underlying reference-based automatic evaluation metrics.
title: Challenges in AI based tumor board case summarization and recommendations

summary: Abnormal body composition at intensive care unit (ICU) admission is associated with worse survival, but it is rarely measured in practice because manual CT analysis is labor-intensive. We conducted a secondary analysis of a single-center prospective cohort of 509 patients who underwent chest CT within 24 h of ICU admission, of whom 475 were included in the final analysis. Open-source AI segmentation was used to quantify body composition, and the resulting features were related to 6-month survival. Risk scores derived from body composition were significantly associated with 6-month survival (p < 0.001, log-rank test). In five-fold cross-validation, the AUC for discriminating survivors from non-survivors was 0.73; when feature selection was accounted for, the AUC was 0.68 by nested cross-validation and 0.69 by bootstrap optimism correction. The study shows that the automated AI-based analysis of admission chest CT yields body composition scores significantly associated with 6-month mortality after ICU admission.
title: AI-assisted chest CT scan analysis of body composition at ICU admission and 6-month mortality
